_note: High-voltage classes in Stanford Cars (verified against the 196 class names). Every location below was read from the cited manufacturer document, never from memory: see docs/hazard-sources.md for pages and hosts. Leave a field null rather than guess. 'Passenger side' is the guide's wording for US left-hand-drive cars. 'schematic' places the battery region on the rescue-sheet drawing; only draw a cable route a guide states.

BMW ActiveHybrid 5 Sedan 2012.battery: Under the luggage compartment trim, in the boot. Up to 385 V.
BMW ActiveHybrid 5 Sedan 2012.hv_cables: Orange insulation. The rescue disconnect is reached from the boot, after lifting out the luggage floor trim.

Chevrolet Silverado 1500 Hybrid Crew Cab.guide_title: GM two-mode hybrid first responder guide
Chevrolet Silverado 1500 Hybrid Crew Cab.battery: In a metal case under the second-row rear seat sub-floor. 300 V, and it cannot be disabled.
Chevrolet Silverado 1500 Hybrid Crew Cab.hv_cables: Orange means high voltage, blue means intermediate voltage. Do not cut the orange 300 V cables.

Chevrolet Tahoe Hybrid SUV 2012.guide_title: GM two-mode hybrid first responder guide
Chevrolet Tahoe Hybrid SUV 2012.battery: In a metal case under the second-row rear seat sub-floor. 300 V, and it cannot be disabled.
Chevrolet Tahoe Hybrid SUV 2012.hv_cables: Orange means high voltage, blue means intermediate voltage. Do not cut the orange 300 V cables.

Chevrolet Malibu Hybrid Sedan 2010.guide_title: GM Malibu Hybrid emergency response guide
Chevrolet Malibu Hybrid Sedan 2010.battery: In the trunk, directly behind the rear passenger seats. 36 V.
Chevrolet Malibu Hybrid Sedan 2010.hv_cables: Blue sheathing, not orange (36-42 V), in a rigid metal conduit where it runs under the car. Do not cut it: arc hazard.

GMC Yukon Hybrid SUV 2012.guide_title: GM two-mode hybrid first responder guide
GMC Yukon Hybrid SUV 2012.battery: In a metal case under the second-row rear seat sub-floor. 300 V, and it cannot be disabled.
GMC Yukon Hybrid SUV 2012.hv_cables: Orange means high voltage, blue means intermediate voltage. Do not cut the orange 300 V cables.

Hyundai Sonata Hybrid Sedan 2012.guide_title: Hyundai Sonata Hybrid emergency response guide
Hyundai Sonata Hybrid Sedan 2012.battery: Behind the rear seat, in the trunk area. 270 V.
Hyundai Sonata Hybrid Sedan 2012.hv_cables: Orange. One runs under the car along the passenger side, from the rear to the engine bay; more in the engine bay.

Fisker Karma Sedan 2012.guide_title: Fisker high-voltage safety and first response guide
Fisker Karma Sedan 2012.battery: Runs along the centre tunnel to behind the rear seats (guide's do-not-cut diagram). About 400 V, live at all times. Manual disconnect under the left rear seat cushion.
Fisker Karma Sedan 2012.hv_cables: Orange insulation, running the length of the car. Do not cut under the car in front of, behind or through the tunnel.

Nissan Leaf Hatchback 2012.battery: Encased in steel and mounted underneath the vehicle. Do not crib under it. Service disconnect on the rear seat floor.
Nissan Leaf Hatchback 2012.hv_cables: All high-voltage harnesses are coated in orange. Routing is shown in the guide's diagram.

Tesla Model S Sedan 2012.guide_title: Tesla Model S 2012-13 emergency response guide
Tesla Model S Sedan 2012.battery: Below the floor, under a floor pan, across a large section of the undercarriage. Never breach it when lifting.
Tesla Model S Sedan 2012.hv_cables: Orange. Routed under the rear seats and inside the rocker panel on the right side front.
